conflicts.title: Thesis scope versus full-platform proposals
conflicts.resolution: Treat thesis outputs as demonstrated methodology and later full-platform structures as post-thesis proposals.

conflicts.title: Six conceptual layers versus fourteen engineering volumes
conflicts.resolution: Retain the six conceptual responsibility layers; map volumes as subordinate engineering groupings rather than layer equivalents.

conflicts.title: Deterministic BGE wording versus LLM semantic reasoning
conflicts.resolution: Require deterministic schemas, validation, and audit envelopes while treating semantic generation as non-deterministic candidate production subject to validation.

conflicts.title: Meta software hierarchy versus Human authority
conflicts.resolution: Human remains the sole adoption authority; software layers may only propose, validate, or enforce adopted decisions.

conflicts.title: Fixed eight-RFC pattern versus risk-based governance
conflicts.resolution: Present fixed and risk-based options without selecting either as Normative Architecture.

conflicts.title: Agent Registry ownership and scope
conflicts.resolution: Bound the Registry to identity and lineage; defer whether it is a Factory subcomponent or independent control-plane service.

conflicts.title: Runtime Governance placement
conflicts.resolution: Preserve logical separation from Product Runtime; defer physical/component placement.

conflicts.title: Evidence Ledger as standalone service
conflicts.resolution: Define evidence responsibility but defer standalone versus shared-service placement.

conflicts.title: Trustworthy Prompt OS versus Agent OS naming
conflicts.resolution: Use Blueprint Compiler/BGE for design-time knowledge compilation and Agent OS for runtime execution; do not treat the thesis compiler as a complete Agent OS.

conflicts.title: VET-C and health-domain contamination risk
conflicts.resolution: Use only generalized thesis methodology and optional general process patterns; prohibit VET-C-specific and health-specific domain promotion.
